name: National Fish Passage Program
summary: US federal funding and technical help for partners that remove dams and other river barriers, replace culverts, restore floodplains or install fishways. Projects are developed with the local Fish and Wildlife Service fish passage biologist before applying.
reporting: Recipients file federal financial reports and programme performance reports, on the schedule set in the notice of award.

eligibility.rule: Not part of Federal or State compensatory mitigation, in-lieu fee programmes or mitigation banks
Fish passage is not already required under an existing Federal or State regulatory programme
No grant funds to build, operate or maintain fish passage at facilities with an active FERC licence or permit
Registered in SAM.gov before applying, unless applying as a natural person
Applicant and key personnel have no SAM.gov exclusion that applies to this programme
For FRIMA funding, work in Pacific Ocean drainages in Oregon, Washington, Montana, Idaho or California

steps: Contact local fish passage programme staff to develop the project
Eligibility and merit review by regional programme staff
Submit the formal application if invited

deadline.text: Closing Date for Applications: 04/30/2027, by 11:59 PM, ET

status.quote: allocated $15 million for the National Fish Passage Program

deadline.quote: Closing Date for Applications: 04/30/2027 Closing Date Explanation Electronically submitted applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 PM, ET, on the listed application due date.

applicant_types.quote: The program seeks and develops projects collaboratively with partners, including but not limited to: State and local agencies, Tribes, non-governmental organizations, other Federal agencies

geography.quote: The program is delivered through U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service) field offices nationwide.

access.quote: Contact a regional NFPP Coordinator in your area for information about program priorities and the application process.

window.quote: Electronically submitted applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 PM, ET, on the listed application due date.

co_finance_required.quote: FRIMA funded projects must source a non-federal match amount (minimum of 35%).

reporting.quote: Submit Federal Financial reports and Program Performance reports.

eligibility.quote: Projects not eligible for program funding include any projects that are part of any Federal or State compensatory mitigation, including in-lieu fee programs and mitigation banks.
Projects are also not eligible if fish passage is a condition provided by existing Federal or State regulatory programs.
program funds may not be used to construct, operate, or maintain fish passage at facilities actively licensed or permitted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
Before applying, all applicants except individuals applying as a natural person must be registered in SAM.gov.

the current list of prohibited or restricted persons or entities in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) Exclusions database. We are prohibited from making an award if a recipient or any key personnel are found ineligible, prohibited, restricted, or otherwise excluded from receiving or participating in an award, as their ineligibility condition applies to this program.

Funds provided to NFPP for the implementation of FRIMA will support the development, improvement, or installation of fish screens, fish passage devices and related features to mitigate impacts on fisheries associated with irrigation water system diversions in Pacific Ocean drainages in Oregon, Washington, Montana, Idaho, and California.

effort.quote: Applicants seeking technical or financial assistance from the National Fish Passage Program are required to contact local program staff BEFORE developing or submitting an application.

Applications in GrantSolutions should be submitted by invitation only after Regional FAC staff determine eligibility (Section Eligibility Review) and review responses to selection criteria (Section Merit Review).
Prior to making an award, the applicant will be assessed for their level of risk per 2 CFR 200.206.
Applicants should not submit applications to GrantSolutions or Grants.gov until they have been invited by program staff.

co_finance.quote: FRIMA funded projects must source a non-federal match amount (minimum of 35%).

after_award.quote: Submit Federal Financial reports and Program Performance reports.
